topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation-driven cancer development and susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations produce cancer through clonal evolution when cellular susceptibility and the surrounding environment permit it.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and challenge explanations that attribute cancer solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens cause DNA damage and mutations through mechanisms that depend on their interaction with cellular processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-causing initiation from promotion that enables initiated cells to proliferate in a supportive environment.

topics.label: Biological context and specificity of carcinogen effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposed cells determines carcinogen susceptibility and consolidate that explanation in a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be identified and tested, emphasizing the evidential strengths and limitations of available methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as risk–benefit judgments.
